scope: Independent software safety and schema tests of the newly authored outer archive verifier. No mathematical proof, novelty clearance, original-code replay or compact-construction experiment is established. Release-specific integration and final tree checks are separate.
tested_boundaries: Boolean versus integer rejection and bounded values
Path traversal, absolute paths, control characters and backslashes
Duplicate JSON keys, floats/nonfinite values, invalid UTF-8 and structural limits
Byte length, SHA-256 and Git-blob identities
Manifest schema, duplicate/self/global entries and file-size limits
Original/public source identity mapping and lossless-chunk declaration
Inherited dependency counts, duplicates and overlap
Fixed trace-result status, no-scientific-replay and no-reconstruction result contracts
Exact scoped file-set closure, missing and extra scoped entries
Symlink files, symlink directories, symlink roots and FIFOs
Bounded regular-file reads and excessive directory width
Bad external manifest anchor rejection with input-byte stability
Required isolated/no-bytecode CLI flags and machine-readable failure results
fixture_policy: All mutation fixtures are synthetic, deterministic and created exclusively in new local directories. They are not publication inputs or archived records. No random generator, network operation, original checker/launcher, model or science computation is used.
reviewed_execution_boundary: The outer helper reads bounded regular files through descriptor-relative POSIX access. It verifies an externally trusted manifest anchor and executes only the hash-pinned new retained-record helper. Archived programs are never imported. It rechecks all selected and inherited bytes after the nested helper; this is not an atomic snapshot against a hostile concurrent filesystem.
limitations: The explicit trusted manifest hash must come from an independently trusted release receipt, commit or inventory.
Public source maps preserve original identities, not the unavailable private original bytes. Exact normalization and source freeze checks occur separately before release.
Saved-record schema and pass flags do not independently prove the mathematical construction or rerun numerical operations.
No package installation, license grant, external communication, remote write or deployment was performed by these tests.
